---
title: "Deriving the Free Energy functional aka the ELBO"
author: "Richard Mason"
date: "2026-08-15"
description: "Deriving the free energy functional starting from Bayes' theorem."
categories: [AI, Variational Inference]
---

One of the approaches to approximate inference that I like is the Free Energy functional, popularised by Friston as a core part of his free energy principle for understanding the brain. The idea is to first rearrange Bayes' rule to focus on the intractable marginal $p(y)$. 

$$p(y) = \frac{p(y|x)p(x)}{p(x|y)}$$

Let $q_{\theta}(x)$ be an arbitrary probability distirbution parameterised by $\theta\in\Theta$. We have the freedom to insert this distribution into the top and bottom of the fraction on the RHS

$$p(y) = \frac{p(y|x)p(x)q_{\theta}(x)}{p(x|y)q_{\theta}(x)}.$$

Next we take logs of both sides and negate, converting the LHS into surprise 

$$-\log{p(y)} = -\log{\frac{p(y|x)p(x)q_{\theta}(x)}{p(x|y)q_{\theta}(x)}}.$$

Then taking the expectation of both sides over $q_{\theta}(x)$ we have

$$-\mathbb{E}_{q_{\theta}(x)}[\log{p(y)}] = -\mathbb{E}_{q_{\theta}(x)}\left[\log{\frac{p(y|x)p(x)q_{\theta}(x)}{p(x|y)q_{\theta}(x)}}\right].$$


The LHS is not a function of $x$ so the integral simplifies 

$$-\mathbb{E}_{q_{\theta}(x)}[\log{p(y)}] = -\int q_{\theta}(x)\log{p(y)}dx = -\log{p(y)} \int q_{\theta}(x)dx = -\log{p(y)}.$$

On the RHS we can choose how to split the terms inside the logarithm 

$$-\mathbb{E}_{q_{\theta}(x)}\left[\log{\frac{p(y|x)p(x)q_{\theta}(x)}{p(x|y)q_{\theta}(x)}}\right] = -\mathbb{E}_{q_{\theta}(x)}\left[\log{\frac{p(y|x)p(x)}{q_{\theta}(x)}}\right]-\mathbb{E}_{q_{\theta}(x)}\left[\log{\frac{q_{\theta}(x)}{p(x|y)}}\right].$$

Recognising the second term as the Kullbach leibler divergence between $q_{\theta}(x)$ and $p(x | y)$ which is always nonnegative we have the inequality

$$-\log{p(y)} \leq -\mathbb{E}_{q_{\theta}(x)}\left[\log{\frac{p(y|x)p(x)}{q_{\theta}(x)}}\right]$$

with equality attained when  $q_{\theta}(x)=p(x | y)$. We can split terms out on the right hand side into an energy term minus an entropy term

$$-\log{p(y)} \leq -\mathbb{E}_{q_{\theta}(x)}\left[\log{p(y|x)p(x)}\right] - H(q_{\theta}(x)) $$

where $H(q_{\theta}(x)) = -\mathbb{E}_{q_{\theta}(x)}\left[\log{q_\theta(x)}\right]$. In other words the surprise of an observation is bounded above by the expectation of the joint probability of $x$ and $y$ occurring under our model and the entropy of the approximating distribution $q_{\theta}(x)$. The natural next questions are how can we choose $q_{\theta}(x)$ to be expressive enough to represent different states of the world yet make the optimisation problem of minimising the resulting functional computationally tractable? These question will be a subject for a subsequent post.
